async def act(page):
    import asyncio

    # Plan:
    # 1) Open the Manage Attributes page (relative goto).
    # 2) Open the "color" attribute for editing by clicking its link.
    # 3) In the attribute edit form, click an "Add Option"-style control if present.
    # 4) Fill the newly-added option textbox with "Brown" (use the last textbox in the form).
    # 5) Save the attribute via the form's Save button.
    # Notes: Use only accessibility-tree-centric selectors (page.get_by_role and .get_by_role on parents).

    # There are no knowledge_base helper functions available for these actions.

    # 1) Go to Manage Attributes
    await page.goto('/index.php/admin/catalog/product_attribute/index/')
    await page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # 2) Open the color attribute edit page. Try several common variants of the attribute link name.
    attribute_clicked = False
    possible_attribute_names = ['color', 'Color', 'Color (color)']
    for name in possible_attribute_names:
        try:
            link = page.get_by_role('link', name=name)
            if await link.count() > 0:
                await link.first.click()
                attribute_clicked = True
                break
        except Exception:
            # ignore and try next
            pass

    if not attribute_clicked:
        # If exact link name not found, try scanning all links for one that contains the substring 'color'.
        # We still stick to get_by_role API: iterate page.get_by_role('link') and check .all_inner_texts()
        try:
            links = page.get_by_role('link')
            total = await links.count()
            for i in range(total):
                l = links.nth(i)
                try:
                    text = (await l.all_inner_texts())[0]
                except Exception:
                    text = ''
                if 'color' in text.lower():
                    await l.click()
                    attribute_clicked = True
                    break
        except Exception:
            pass

    if not attribute_clicked:
        raise Exception('Could not find or open the color attribute for editing')

    await page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # 3) In the attribute edit UI, target the form/group that contains option controls
    form = page.get_by_role('form')
    if await form.count() == 0:
        # Fallback to a generic group if a formal <form> role isn't available
        form = page.get_by_role('group')

    # 4) Try to click an "Add Option" button/link inside the form if present
    add_clicked = False
    add_candidates = ['Add Option', 'Add New', 'Add New Row', 'Add New Option']
    for name in add_candidates:
        try:
            btn = form.get_by_role('button', name=name)
            if await btn.count() > 0:
                await btn.first.click()
                add_clicked = True
                break
        except Exception:
            pass

    if not add_clicked:
        for name in add_candidates:
            try:
                lnk = form.get_by_role('link', name=name)
                if await lnk.count() > 0:
                    await lnk.first.click()
                    add_clicked = True
                    break
            except Exception:
                pass

    # It's possible the UI already has an empty option row without needing to click Add.
    await asyncio.sleep(0.8)

    # 5) Fill the last textbox inside the form with the label 'Brown'
    textboxes = form.get_by_role('textbox')
    tb_count = await textboxes.count()
    if tb_count == 0:
        # If no textboxes found in the form, try to find any textbox on the page as a last resort
        page_textboxes = page.get_by_role('textbox')
        page_tb_count = await page_textboxes.count()
        if page_tb_count == 0:
            raise Exception('No textboxes found to enter the new option label')
        await page_textboxes.nth(page_tb_count - 1).fill('Brown')
    else:
        await textboxes.nth(tb_count - 1).fill('Brown')

    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

    # 6) Save the attribute via a Save button within the form if available, otherwise at page level
    saved = False
    save_candidates = ['Save Attribute', 'Save Attribute(s)', 'Save']
    for name in save_candidates:
        try:
            btn = form.get_by_role('button', name=name)
            if await btn.count() > 0:
                await btn.first.click()
                saved = True
                break
        except Exception:
            pass

    if not saved:
        for name in save_candidates:
            try:
                btn = page.get_by_role('button', name=name)
                if await btn.count() > 0:
                    await btn.first.click()
                    saved = True
                    break
            except Exception:
                pass

    if not saved:
        raise Exception('Could not find a Save button to persist the new option')

    await page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # Completed: the new color option 'Brown' should now be added to the color attribute.
    return
step_by_step_reasoning:
I will add the 'Brown' option to the global color attribute so it becomes available for the product. There are no knowledge_base helper functions available for these actions, so I won't call any. Plan:
1) Open the Manage Attributes page via a relative goto to /index.php/admin/catalog/product_attribute/index/. Using a relative goto avoids relying on menu navigation that can be ambiguous.
2) Find and click the 'color' attribute link. I try multiple likely names (case variants). If an exact link isn't found I iterate over all links and click the first whose visible text contains 'color'. All link accesses use page.get_by_role to adhere to accessibility-tree-centric selectors.
3) Once on the attribute edit page, I target the form (page.get_by_role('form')) or fallback to a generic group. I try to click an "Add Option"-type control inside that form (several candidate names) using form.get_by_role('button'/'link', name=...). This matches the guidance to use the full parent.get_by_role(...) path for generic buttons.
4) I then fill the last textbox inside the form with 'Brown' (or the last textbox on the page as a final fallback). This adds the new option label.
5) I save the attribute by clicking a Save button scoped to the form first, then the page.

I used only page.get_by_role and parent.get_by_role selectors (with .nth and .count) and avoided CSS or page.locator selectors, addressing the prior errors. I added short sleeps and networkidle waits to let the UI settle between steps.
